av_event.line_text: Ryan: Bruno's only three. Eats everything. Shoes, remote.
av_event.what: In the background behind Ryan, a brown-and-white staffie cross wanders in through the half-open hallway door, climbs up onto the dark grey settee, turns round twice and lies down on the folded throw. Ryan doesn't look round.

text:
A: Alright. Tracey, Sittingbourne.
B: Alright. Ryan. Castleford.
A: You're the mechanic, ain't you? Someone said there was one.
B: Yeah. Who said?
A: Woman from Gosport. Joanne. She said you'd sorted her sister's clutch out. Sort of.
B: Told her six hundred weren't mad.
A: Well, you've made her day. Right, while I've got you. My other half's got a Transit, about twelve years old, and it keeps cutting out at junctions. Just dies. Starts again after a minute. He's had it at a bloke's twice and it's still doing it. Last week I had to go and get him from Faversham.
B: Diesel?
A: Yeah.
B: Could be a few things. Fuel filter if it's not been done. Or the crank sensor, they go on them and it does exactly that, cuts out, then starts when it's cooled a bit. Cheap part. Tell him to get it plugged in when it's just done it, not after.
A: Crank sensor. I'll tell him. He'll say he knew.
B: They always do.
A: Do you like it, the garage?
B: It's alright. Busy. Don't like customers.
A: Same. I'm on shelves at a supermarket, early mornings. I'd do it twice as quick if nobody stopped me to ask where the gravy is.
B: Ha. Yeah.
A: Got a dog? You look like a dog person.
B: Staffie cross. Bruno.
A: Get out. I've got a staffie. Roxy. She's twelve, her hips have gone. Vet wants her on tablets for life and they're forty quid a month.
B: Bruno's only three. Eats everything. Shoes, remote.
A: Roxy was like that. Ate a whole tray of sausage rolls off the side at Christmas once, Dean's mum's. Never forgiven her.
B: Sounds about right.
A: Going anywhere this year?
B: Chloe's booking summat. Tenerife, maybe. She does all that.
A: Tenerife's good. Been four times. Get all-inclusive and don't move.
B: That's the plan.
A: That puzzle at the start was daft, weren't it.
B: Didn't finish it.
A: No one did, apart from her in Hornchurch.
B: Had her an' all.
A: Yeah?
B: Told me I needed a spreadsheet.
A: Ha! Course she did.
B: She weren't wrong, to be fair.
A: No, probably not. Still.
